**Context:** 
Paima Studios merged into the Midnight Foundation, and Paima Engine was rebranded as EffectStream. We have rewritten the entire codebase from scratch - this is the third version. We listened to feedback, followed better practices, and improved overall quality. These events are why we are delivering now, but everything has been updated for the present. "Paima Primitives" are now called "EffectStream Primitives" after the rebrand; the API surface is unchanged in spirit — a primitive emits typed events into a state machine, and a game reacts to them in an `addStateTransition` handler. The PoolDelegation primitive plus the `Stm` + `World.resolve()` pattern in the cardano-delegation template together provide the queryable, reactive delegation API the milestone scoped. Even though we have delivered with EffectStream and Dolos/UTxORPC, the original Paima Engine code is available at https://github.com/PaimaStudios/paima-engine. This Milestone is provided after the fact, so it contains further reach than M3. New site https://effectstream.github.io/home/

**A. Output: A documented Primitive that lets games query and react to delegation changes**
Acceptance criteria: Create and document a "Paima Primitive" that allows games to query and update based off delegation changes and all related utility functions. Delivered as the `CardanoPoolDelegation` primitive plus the cardano-delegation template's state machine wiring. The primitive emits a `{ address, pool, epoch }` payload into a typed grammar; a game subscribes by registering a state transition handler that fires on every delegation change. Utility functions for querying current delegation state are provided as pgtyped queries: `getDelegations`, `getDelegationsByPool`, `getDelegationsByAddress`, and `getPoolStats`. These cover both reactive logic (handler fires when delegation changes) and pull logic (query current state at any block).

ms.promise:
・Allow Paima batchers to check which pool an address is delegating to and include documentation on how to modify the batcher to use this configuration in the Paima engine docs

The main use-case we aim to enable is to power features such as stake pool being able to spin up batchers that provide free transactions for delegators of to their pool
ms.criteria: An easy-to-use configuring system to allow Paima batchers to treat users differently depending on which pool they are delegating to
ms.report:
NOTE: we have updated this PoC with 
(1) a video for this specific milestone 
(2) simplified documentation 
(3) Notes from the Cardano Directive (in the comments and notes below)
BRIEF
This milestone delivers pool-aware batchers: an easy-to-use configuration system that lets a batcher treat users differently depending on which Cardano stake pool they delegate to. The headline use-case works end to end - a stake pool operator can spin up a batcher that provides free transactions for delegators of their pool. Delivered as the DelegationAwareBatcherAdapter: it extends the default L2 adapter with a validateInput method that queries the delegations table (written by the Cardano sync node over Dolos/UTxORPC) and checks the user's current delegation against a configured ENABLED_POOLS array of pool operator keyhashes. Delegators of enabled pools get free transactions (fee 0); everyone else is rejected at the HTTP layer before their input enters the queue. Configuration is that single array - an SPO sets it to their pool's keyhash and the batcher does the rest.

NOTE: Due to short timelines for this project, we have submitted this milestone before the previous was approved. This was discussed with the Cardano Directive, and a formal statement was added at the end of the PoA. This milestone is totally independent and does not depend in any way on previous milestones.
FOR REVIEWERS
Thanks for the previous review. This submission was partially reviewed before this PoA update. We have improved the format, added videos, and content for an easier explanation of the milestones. We have also added a statement by the Catalyst Directive that helped us review the scope and other important points, info in NOTES.
BRIEF
This milestone delivers games that leverage Cardano stake delegation, with documentation, an SPO onboarding channel, and a public feedback loop. The original scope asked for at least one public game with at least one stake-pool integration; the delivery is materially broader: stake delegation became the consensus weight of an entire chain. Four production games (Safe Solver, Kachina Kolosseum, Block Kart Legends, Dust-2-Dust) run on Midnight, a Cardano partner chain whose validator set is selected from registered Cardano SPOs. Cardano SPOs register permissionlessly as Midnight block producers via the Partner Chains Toolkit, and the Ariadne committee-selection algorithm reads those registrations and the delegation stake behind them from Cardano's ledger every epoch. So the same delegation certificate that earns a user Cardano staking rewards also weights block production on the partner chain their games run on - every transaction in every game on Midnight is produced by a committee drawn from Cardano stake pools, with delegation as the input.
